images.caption:
The Boeing Airplane Company got its first big military order when its "C" model seaplane was accepted as a trainer by the U.S. Navy during World War I. The company opened a new plant on the west side of the Duwamish River, south of Seattle, to handle all this new business. This photo, taken in April 1918, shows the new factory, Plant 1 of the Boeing Airplane Company.
Caption on image: 4-16-1918.

Typed on sleeve: Boeing Plant, April 6 [sic], 1918. Located the west side of the Duwamish River, opposite Patterson-McDonald Shipbuilding Company, whose address was 5917 E. Marginal Way (1919 City Directory). Michigan St. Bridge ") in center. Address of Seattle Machine Works, Plant 2, is East Marginal Way near Myrtle St. Original no. 54.

Caption by MOHAI staff.

images.filename: Men assembling wooden wings at Boeing Airplane Company, 1922 (MOHAI 7207).jpg
images.caption:
In 1921, the Boeing Airplane Company won a large government contract to build 200 single-seater MB-3A fighter planes for the U. S. Army. By the end of 1922, workers had completed the work and had also designed, built and refurbished several other kinds of planes. This helped keep the company open during the business slump that followed World War I.
This 1922 photo shows men building the framework for airplane wings at the Boeing Airplane Company. After the men completed the wooden framework, the women in the sewing room covered the wings with linen fabric.
Photo is one of four in a panorama.
Subjects (LCTGM): Airplane industry; Airplane wings; Boeing Airplane Company; Men--Employment
